question: What known full names belong to superheroes tied for the highest strength attribute value?
gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT s.full_name FROM superhero AS s JOIN hero_attribute AS ha ON ha.hero_id = s.id JOIN attribute AS a ON a.id = ha.attribute_id WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Strength' AND ha.attribute_value = ( SELECT MAX(ha2.attribute_value) FROM hero_attribute AS ha2 JOIN attribute AS a2 ON a2.id = ha2.attribute_id WHERE a2.attribute_name = 'Strength' ) AND s.full_name IS NOT NULL AND s.full_name <> '-' ORDER BY s.full_name ASC

question: List superheroes whose known eye, hair and skin colours are all the same, along with any recorded publisher name.
gold_sql: SELECT s.superhero_name, p.publisher_name FROM superhero AS s LEFT JOIN publisher AS p ON p.id = s.publisher_id JOIN colour AS c ON c.id = s.eye_colour_id WHERE s.eye_colour_id = s.hair_colour_id AND s.eye_colour_id = s.skin_colour_id AND c.colour <> 'No Colour'

question: Among all female superheroes, what percentage have blue skin? Round to two decimals.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN co.colour = 'Blue' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 2) FROM superhero AS s JOIN gender AS g ON g.id = s.gender_id LEFT JOIN colour AS co ON co.id = s.skin_colour_id WHERE g.gender = 'Female'

question: Among all female superheroes, what percentage were published by Marvel Comics? Round to two decimal places.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 2) FROM superhero AS s JOIN gender AS g ON s.gender_id = g.id LEFT JOIN publisher AS p ON s.publisher_id = p.id WHERE g.gender = 'Female'

question: I'm setting a typical weight for a green-skinned creature class. Can you tell me the average weight in kg of the heroes with green skin? Count only heroes whose weight is known, and give me one number rounded to one decimal place.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(T1.weight_kg), 1) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN colour AS T2 ON T1.skin_colour_id = T2.id WHERE T2.colour = 'Green' AND T1.weight_kg > 0
evidence: Green skin means the hero's skin colour is green.

question: For my 'giants of the genre' feature, I want to headline how varied the abilities of the tallest heroes are. How many different superpowers appear among the ten tallest superheroes? Rank heroes by height and take the top ten; if several heroes tie at the tenth-tallest height, include all of them. A hero counts among the ten tallest even if no powers are on file for them. Please give me just that single number.
gold_sql: WITH top10 AS (SELECT id FROM superhero ORDER BY height_cm DESC LIMIT 10) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T3.power_name) AS superpowers FROM top10 JOIN hero_power T2 ON top10.id = T2.hero_id JOIN superpower T3 ON T2.power_id = T3.id
evidence: superpower = an ability such as Agility or Accelerated Healing, as named in the superpower list

question: Hey, following up on my count of the God / Eternal heroes – among those who are male, what's the average number of superpowers per hero? Just give me the average rounded to two decimal places.
gold_sql: WITH power_counts AS (SELECT s.id, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hero_power AS hp WHERE hp.hero_id = s.id) AS power_count FROM superhero AS s INNER JOIN race AS r ON s.race_id = r.id INNER JOIN gender AS g ON s.gender_id = g.id WHERE r.race = 'God / Eternal' AND g.gender = 'Male') SELECT ROUND(AVG(power_count), 2) AS average_superpowers FROM power_counts
evidence: A superpower is any power linked to a hero.

question: For my cryokinesis page, I want to know how broad the power portfolios are around ice-powered heroes. Consider all heroes who share at least one superpower with a cryokinesis holder - including the cryokinesis holders themselves, since they share cryokinesis with each other. What is the average number of superpowers these heroes have, rounded to one decimal place? Please send back just that single number.
gold_sql: WITH sharers AS (SELECT DISTINCT hp2.hero_id FROM hero_power hp1 JOIN hero_power hp2 ON hp2.power_id = hp1.power_id WHERE hp1.hero_id IN (SELECT hero_id FROM hero_power WHERE power_id = (SELECT id FROM superpower WHERE power_name = 'Cryokinesis'))), counts AS (SELECT hero_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM hero_power WHERE hero_id IN (SELECT hero_id FROM sharers) GROUP BY hero_id) SELECT ROUND(AVG(cnt), 1) AS avg_superpower_count FROM counts
evidence: Cryokinesis is the superpower to generate and control ice.

question: What is the average weight, in kg, of the heroes who belong to races in which no hero is female? Heroes whose weight is not recorded should not count toward the average. I just need that single value.
gold_sql: SELECT AVG(T1.weight_kg) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN race AS T2 ON T1.race_id = T2.id WHERE T1.weight_kg > 0 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM superhero AS T3 INNER JOIN gender AS T4 ON T3.gender_id = T4.id WHERE T3.race_id = T2.id AND T4.gender = 'Female')
evidence: female: the hero's gender is female

question: For a licensing survey of non-DC heroic characters, I need a single total count of superheroes whose alignment is Good and who are not published by DC Comics. Just that one number, please.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS hero_count FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN alignment AS T2 ON T1.alignment_id = T2.id WHERE T2.alignment = 'Good' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM publisher AS T3 WHERE T3.id = T1.publisher_id AND T3.publisher_name = 'DC Comics')
evidence: Good means the hero's alignment is Good; DC Comics means the publisher named DC Comics.

question: Which race is the most common among the superheroes published by the same publisher as the superhero whose full name is Charles Chandler? I'd like, for that publisher's superheroes only, the name of the most common race and the count of that publisher's superheroes of that race. Ignore any superhero with no race recorded. If several races tie for most common, list every tied race with its count.
gold_sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT r.race AS race, COUNT(*) AS hero_count FROM superhero AS s INNER JOIN race AS r ON s.race_id = r.id WHERE s.publisher_id = (SELECT publisher_id FROM superhero WHERE full_name = 'Charles Chandler') AND r.race <> '-' GROUP BY r.id, r.race) SELECT race, hero_count FROM counts WHERE hero_count = (SELECT MAX(hero_count) FROM counts)
evidence: Race: the superhero's species or type, e.g. Human, Mutant, Alien.

question: I'm writing a power-profile feature on heroes with super speed or death touch. Can you give me one number: the average intelligence score of the superheroes who have either of those powers? Round it to one decimal place, and only count the heroes who actually have an intelligence score in the database.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(v), 1) AS average_intelligence FROM (SELECT DISTINCT T1.id, T4.attribute_value AS v FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN hero_power AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.hero_id INNER JOIN superpower AS T3 ON T2.power_id = T3.id INNER JOIN hero_attribute AS T4 ON T4.hero_id = T1.id INNER JOIN attribute AS T5 ON T4.attribute_id = T5.id WHERE T3.power_name IN ('Super Speed', 'Death Touch') AND T5.attribute_name = 'Intelligence')
evidence: "Super speed" and "death touch" are superpower names as used in the database; "intelligence" is the hero attribute by that name.

question: I'm putting together a physical profile of the green-skinned villain corner of the universe for a fan wiki page. Could you tell me the average height in centimetres and the average weight in kilograms of the green-skinned villains? Please average only over the characters whose measurement is actually on record - a character with no recorded height or weight shouldn't drag the average down - and round each average to two decimals. I just need those two numbers.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN T1.height_cm > 0 THEN T1.height_cm END), 2) AS avg_height_cm, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN T1.weight_kg > 0 THEN T1.weight_kg END), 2) AS avg_weight_kg FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN alignment AS T2 ON T1.alignment_id = T2.id INNER JOIN colour AS T3 ON T1.skin_colour_id = T3.id WHERE T2.alignment = 'Bad' AND T3.colour = 'Green'
evidence: By 'villain' I mean a character whose alignment is Bad, and by 'green-skinned' I mean a character whose skin colour is Green. Height in centimetres and weight in kilograms are the character's height_cm and weight_kg as commonly understood physical measurements.

question: I'm profiling publisher rosters and now want to look at the physical build of George Lucas's heroes. What is the average height of the heroes he created, in centimetres, and their average weight, in kilograms? Please round each average to one decimal place, and only include heroes whose height (for the height average) or weight (for the weight average) is actually known.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.height_cm > 0 THEN s.height_cm END), 1) AS average_height_cm, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.weight_kg > 0 THEN s.weight_kg END), 1) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero AS s INNER JOIN publisher AS p ON s.publisher_id = p.id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'George Lucas'

question: I'm picking powers for a lightweight male hero archetype. How many different superpowers are held by at least one male superhero who weighs under 70 kilograms? Heroes whose weight isn't recorded shouldn't count as weighing under 70.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT hp.power_id) AS power_count FROM superhero AS s JOIN hero_power AS hp ON hp.hero_id = s.id JOIN superpower AS sp ON sp.id = hp.power_id JOIN gender AS g ON g.id = s.gender_id WHERE g.gender = 'Male' AND s.weight_kg > 0 AND s.weight_kg < 70;

question: I want to know about the lightest superhero whose weight has actually been recorded. Among all heroes sharing that lightest weight, give me the largest number of superpowers any of them has. If such a hero has no powers, that counts as 0. Please return just that one number.
gold_sql: SELECT MAX(cnt) AS power_count FROM (SELECT COUNT(hp.power_id) AS cnt FROM superhero AS h LEFT JOIN hero_power hp ON h.id = hp.hero_id WHERE h.weight_kg = (SELECT MIN(weight_kg) FROM superhero WHERE weight_kg > 0) GROUP BY h.id)
evidence: A superpower is one power a hero has, identified by its name.

question: I'm auditing identity info on our hero profile pages. How many neutral-alignment heroes have a known full name? Just give me the count.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS neutral_heroes_with_known_full_name FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN alignment AS T2 ON T1.alignment_id = T2.id WHERE T2.alignment = 'Neutral' AND T1.full_name IS NOT NULL AND T1.full_name <> '-'
evidence: By "full name" I mean the hero's real-world identity name, not the superhero/costume name.

question: I'm building a profile page crediting the fastest characters. Among all superheroes that share the top Speed attribute value (everyone tied at the highest Speed value counts), can you list the ones whose real name is known? For each, I need the superhero name and the full name — the civilian identity behind the mask — and nothing else. Please leave out anyone whose real name isn't identifiable.
gold_sql: SELECT s.superhero_name, s.full_name FROM superhero AS s JOIN hero_attribute AS h ON h.hero_id = s.id JOIN attribute AS a ON a.id = h.attribute_id WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Speed' AND h.attribute_value = ( SELECT MAX(h2.attribute_value) FROM hero_attribute AS h2 JOIN attribute AS a2 ON a2.id = h2.attribute_id WHERE a2.attribute_name = 'Speed') AND s.full_name IS NOT NULL AND s.full_name <> '-' ORDER BY s.superhero_name

question: I'm looking at how designers pair hair and eye colours. For every eye colour that appears on at least one brown-haired hero, how many heroes have that eye colour while their hair is NOT brown? Just give me each eye colour and that count, listing the eye colour with the highest count first. If two eye colours have the same count, the one whose name comes first alphabetically should come first.
gold_sql: WITH cohort AS (SELECT DISTINCT s.eye_colour_id AS eid FROM superhero AS s INNER JOIN colour AS h ON s.hair_colour_id = h.id WHERE h.colour = 'Brown') SELECT c.colour AS eye_colour, COUNT(CASE WHEN h.colour <> 'Brown' THEN 1 END) AS heroes FROM cohort AS t INNER JOIN colour AS c ON c.id = t.eid LEFT JOIN superhero AS s ON s.eye_colour_id = t.eid LEFT JOIN colour AS h ON h.id = s.hair_colour_id GROUP BY c.colour ORDER BY heroes DESC, eye_colour
evidence: By a brown-haired hero I mean a hero whose hair colour is Brown.

question: I'm comparing the builds of heroes whose power sets overlap with 3-D Man's. What is the average weight in kg of the heroes other than 3-D Man that share at least one superpower with him? Please round it to two decimal places, leave out any heroes whose weight isn't recorded, and return just that single number.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(weight_kg), 2) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name <> '3-D Man' AND weight_kg > 0 AND id IN (SELECT hero_id FROM hero_power WHERE power_id IN (SELECT power_id FROM hero_power WHERE hero_id = (SELECT id FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name = '3-D Man')))

question: Among superheroes whose weight is not recorded, how many more have the 'No Colour' eye category than have blue eyes? I want a single whole number: the count of 'No Colour' eyes minus the count of blue eyes in that group - it can be negative if blue is more common. Please give me just that one number, with no other results or breakdowns.
gold_sql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN co.colour = 'No Colour' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN co.colour = 'Blue' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS diff FROM superhero AS s JOIN colour AS co ON co.id = s.eye_colour_id WHERE s.weight_kg = 0 OR s.weight_kg IS NULL
evidence: 'No Colour' is an eye category meaning the hero's eye colour is unspecified.

question: Among carcinogenic molecules with at least one single bond, what is the average number of single bonds per molecule?
gold_sql: SELECT AVG(single_bond_count) FROM (SELECT b.molecule_id, COUNT(*) AS single_bond_count FROM bond AS b JOIN molecule AS m ON m.molecule_id = b.molecule_id WHERE m.label = '+' AND b.bond_type = '-' GROUP BY b.molecule_id) AS per_molecule
evidence: In this dataset, '+' denotes a carcinogenic molecule and '-' denotes a single bond.

question: Which elements have the fewest atom occurrences across non-carcinogenic molecules? Include all elements tied for the minimum.
gold_sql: WITH counts AS ( SELECT a.element, COUNT(*) AS n FROM atom AS a JOIN molecule AS m ON m.molecule_id = a.molecule_id WHERE m.label = '-' GROUP BY a.element ) SELECT element FROM counts WHERE n = (SELECT MIN(n) FROM counts) ORDER BY element
evidence: A '-' carcinogenicity label means non-carcinogenic.

question: What is the most common bond type in molecule TR010, and is that molecule carcinogenic? Return the bond type and YES or NO.
gold_sql: SELECT b.bond_type, CASE WHEN m.label = '+' THEN 'YES' ELSE 'NO' END FROM bond AS b JOIN molecule AS m ON m.molecule_id = b.molecule_id WHERE b.molecule_id = 'TR010' GROUP BY b.bond_type, m.label ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, b.bond_type LIMIT 1
evidence: In this dataset, a molecule labeled '+' is carcinogenic; a molecule labeled '-' is not.

question: I want to know whether molecular saturation is associated with carcinogenicity in our compound library. Please report, for molecules in which every bond is a single bond: the number of carcinogenic molecules minus the number of non-carcinogenic molecules. And for all other molecules: the same difference (carcinogenic count minus non-carcinogenic count). Rules: label '+' means the molecule is carcinogenic; label '-' means non-carcinogenic; bond type '-' denotes a single bond; each molecule belongs to exactly one of the two groups.
gold_sql: SELECT (SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN m.label = '+' THEN 1 ELSE -1 END) FROM molecule m WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bond b WHERE b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND b.bond_type <> '-')) AS diff_molecules_with_only_single_bonds, (SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN m.label = '+' THEN 1 ELSE -1 END) FROM molecule m WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bond b WHERE b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND b.bond_type <> '-')) AS diff_other_molecules
evidence: In the labels, '+' indicates a carcinogenic molecule and '-' indicates a non-carcinogenic molecule; for bond types, '-' indicates a single bond.

question: Among the molecules labeled '+' (carcinogenic), which chemical element is the most common among the atoms that take part in at least one bond? Also give the percentage of all atoms in those '+' molecules that this element accounts for, rounded to two decimal places. Count the percentage over every atom of the '+' molecules, whether or not it takes part in a bond. If several elements tie for most common, report each of them.
gold_sql: WITH plus_atoms AS (SELECT a.atom_id, a.element FROM atom a JOIN molecule m ON m.molecule_id = a.molecule_id WHERE m.label = '+'), bonded AS (SELECT atom_id, element FROM plus_atoms WHERE atom_id IN (SELECT atom_id FROM connected) OR atom_id IN (SELECT atom_id2 FROM connected)), bonded_counts AS (SELECT element, COUNT(*) AS n FROM bonded GROUP BY element), top AS (SELECT MAX(n) AS mx FROM bonded_counts), all_counts AS (SELECT element, COUNT(*) AS na FROM plus_atoms GROUP BY element), total AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS tot FROM plus_atoms) SELECT bc.element, ROUND(100.0 * ac.na / t.tot, 2) AS pct FROM bonded_counts bc JOIN top ON bc.n = top.mx JOIN all_counts ac ON ac.element = bc.element CROSS JOIN total t ORDER BY bc.element

question: I want to know how widely chlorine atoms bond to other atoms across the toxicology database. Please give me a single number: the count of atoms that bond with chlorine atoms. Nothing else.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a1.element = 'cl' THEN c.atom_id2 ELSE c.atom_id END) AS bonded_atoms FROM connected AS c JOIN atom AS a1 ON c.atom_id = a1.atom_id JOIN atom AS a2 ON c.atom_id2 = a2.atom_id WHERE a1.element = 'cl' OR a2.element = 'cl'
evidence: Chlorine means the element recorded under the code cl.

question: I'm studying bond patterns in compounds that are not carcinogenic. For each element, how many double or triple bonds join a carbon atom to an atom of that element, across all non-carcinogenic molecules? Give me one row per element with the element and its count of such bonds—nothing else.
gold_sql: SELECT a2.element AS element, COUNT(DISTINCT c.bond_id) AS bond_count FROM connected c JOIN bond b ON c.bond_id = b.bond_id JOIN atom a1 ON c.atom_id = a1.atom_id JOIN atom a2 ON c.atom_id2 = a2.atom_id JOIN molecule m ON b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id WHERE m.label = '-' AND a1.element = 'c' AND b.bond_type != '-' GROUP BY a2.element ORDER BY a2.element
evidence: A molecule labeled '-' is not carcinogenic; a molecule labeled '+' is carcinogenic.

question: I'm profiling the compound library and want to size the fully saturated portion of each element's atom population - atoms attached only by single bonds behave differently from unsaturated sites. For each element symbol in the database, how many atoms are connected only by single bonds and never part of any multiple bond? Please give me one row per element symbol with the element symbol and the number of such atoms, sorted alphabetically by element symbol. This should cover all compounds in the database. Note that an atom with no bonds at all doesn't count as being connected by single bonds, so exclude those.
gold_sql: WITH per_atom AS (SELECT a.atom_id AS atom_id, a.element AS element, CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM connected AS c WHERE c.atom_id = a.atom_id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM connected AS c JOIN bond AS b ON b.bond_id = c.bond_id WHERE c.atom_id = a.atom_id AND b.bond_type <> '-') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS saturated FROM atom AS a) SELECT element, SUM(saturated) AS atoms FROM per_atom GROUP BY element ORDER BY element
evidence: A single bond is a bond between two atoms sharing exactly one electron pair, denoted by the bond-type symbol '-'. A multiple bond is a double or triple bond, i.e. a bond between two atoms sharing more than one electron pair.

question: In the toxicology compound database, which elements take part in a triple bond, and how widely are they distributed across the tested compounds? For each such element, give me its element symbol and the number of molecules that contain that element. Order the results from the most widespread element to the least; where two elements have equal counts, list them alphabetically by element symbol.
gold_sql: SELECT a.element AS element, COUNT(DISTINCT a.molecule_id) AS n_molecules FROM atom AS a WHERE a.element IN (SELECT at.element FROM bond AS b JOIN connected AS c ON b.bond_id = c.bond_id JOIN atom AS at ON c.atom_id = at.atom_id WHERE b.bond_type = '#') GROUP BY a.element ORDER BY n_molecules DESC, a.element
evidence: The '#' bond-type symbol denotes a triple bond.
